description: Manage route tables for AWS Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs).

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: gateway_id
parameters.description: The ID of the gateway to associate with the route table. If gateway_id is 'None' or '', gateway will be disassociated with the route table.

parameters.name: lookup
parameters.description: Look up route table by either tags or by route_table_id. If lookup=tag and tags is not specified then no lookup for an existing route table is performed and a new route table will be created. When using lookup=tag, multiple matches being found will result in a failure and no changes will be made. To change the tags of a route table use lookup=id. vpc_id must be specified when lookup=tag. Choices: "tag" ← (default) "id"

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: propagating_vgw_ids
parameters.description: Enable route propagation from virtual gateways specified by ID.

parameters.name: purge_routes
parameters.description: Purge existing routes that are not found in routes. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: purge_subnets
parameters.description: Purge existing subnets that are not found in subnets. Ignored unless the subnets option is supplied. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: route_table_id
parameters.description: The ID of the route table to update or delete. Required when lookup=id.

parameters.name: routes
parameters.description: List of routes in the route table. Routes are specified as dicts containing the keys dest and one of gateway_id, instance_id, network_interface_id, transit_gateway_id, or vpc_peering_connection_id. The value of dest is used for the destination match. It may be a IPv4 CIDR block or a IPv6 CIDR block. If gateway_id is specified, you can refer to the VPC’s IGW by using the value igw. Routes are required for present states. Default: []

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Create or destroy the VPC route table. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: subnets
parameters.description: An array of subnets to add to this route table. Subnets may be specified by either subnet ID, Name tag, or by a CIDR such as ‘10.0.0.0/24’ or ‘fd00::/8’.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary representing the tags to be applied to the resource. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: vpc_id
parameters.description: VPC ID of the VPC in which to create the route table. Required when state=present or lookup=tag.

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.

# Basic creation example:
- name: Set up public subnet route table
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_route_table:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
    region: us-west-1
    tags:
      Name: Public
    subnets:
      - "{{ jumpbox_subnet.subnet.id }}"
      - "{{ frontend_subnet.subnet.id }}"
      - "{{ vpn_subnet.subnet_id }}"
    routes:
      - dest: 0.0.0.0/0
        gateway_id: "{{ igw.gateway_id }}"
      - dest: ::/0
        gateway_id: "{{ igw.gateway_id }}"
      - dest: 0.0.0.0/0
        gateway_id: "{{ transit_gateway_id }}"
  register: public_route_table

- name: Create VPC gateway
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_igw:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
  register: vpc_igw

- name: Create gateway route table
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_route_table:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
    tags:
      Name: Gateway route table
    gateway_id: "{{ vpc_igw.gateway_id }}"
  register: gateway_route_table

- name: Disassociate gateway from route table
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_route_table:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
    tags:
      Name: Gateway route table
    gateway_id: None
  register: gateway_route_table

- name: Set up NAT-protected route table
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_route_table:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
    region: us-west-1
    tags:
      Name: Internal
    subnets:
      - "{{ application_subnet.subnet.id }}"
      - 'Database Subnet'
      - '10.0.0.0/8'
    routes:
      - dest: 0.0.0.0/0
        instance_id: "{{ nat.instance_id }}"
  register: nat_route_table

- name: delete route table
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_route_table:
    vpc_id: vpc-1245678
    region: us-west-1
    route_table_id: "{{ route_table.id }}"
    lookup: id
    state: absent

return_values.name: route_table
return_values.description: Route Table result. Returned: always

return_values.name: associations
return_values.description: List of associations between the route table and one or more subnets or a gateway. Returned: always

return_values.name: association_state
return_values.description: The state of the association. Returned: always

return_values.name: state
return_values.description: The state of the association. Returned: always Sample: "associated"

return_values.name: state_message
return_values.description: Additional information about the state of the association. Returned: when available Sample: "Creating association"

return_values.name: gateway_id
return_values.description: ID of the internet gateway or virtual private gateway. Returned: when route table is a gateway route table Sample: "igw-03312309"

return_values.name: main
return_values.description: Whether this is the main route table. Returned: always Sample: false

return_values.name: route_table_association_id
return_values.description: ID of association between route table and subnet. Returned: always Sample: "rtbassoc-ab47cfc3"

return_values.name: route_table_id
return_values.description: ID of the route table. Returned: always Sample: "rtb-bf779ed7"

return_values.name: subnet_id
return_values.description: ID of the subnet. Returned: when route table is a subnet route table Sample: "subnet-82055af9"

return_values.name: id
return_values.description: ID of the route table (same as route_table.route_table_id for backwards compatibility). Returned: always Sample: "rtb-bf779ed7"

return_values.name: owner_id
return_values.description: AWS account owning resource. Returned: success Sample: "123456789012"

return_values.name: propagating_vgws
return_values.description: List of Virtual Private Gateways propagating routes. Returned: always Sample: []

return_values.name: routes
return_values.description: List of routes in the route table. Returned: always

return_values.name: carrier_gateway_id
return_values.description: ID of the Carrier gateway. Returned: when the route is via a Carrier gateway Sample: "local"

return_values.name: destination_cidr_block
return_values.description: IPv4 CIDR block of destination Returned: always Sample: "10.228.228.0/22"

return_values.name: destination_ipv6_cidr_block
return_values.description: IPv6 CIDR block of destination Returned: when the route includes an IPv6 destination Sample: "2600:1f1c:1b3:8f00:8000::/65"

return_values.name: instance_id
return_values.description: ID of a NAT instance. Returned: when the route is via an EC2 instance Sample: "i-abcd123456789"

return_values.name: instance_owner_id
return_values.description: AWS account owning the NAT instance. Returned: when the route is via an EC2 instance Sample: "123456789012"

return_values.name: nat_gateway_id
return_values.description: ID of the NAT gateway. Returned: when the route is via a NAT gateway Sample: "local"

return_values.name: origin
return_values.description: mechanism through which the route is in the table. Returned: always Sample: "CreateRouteTable"

return_values.name: transit_gateway_id
return_values.description: ID of the Transit gateway. Returned: when the route is via a Transit gateway Sample: "tgw-123456789012"

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: Tags applied to the route table. Returned: always Sample: {"Name": "Public route table", "Public": "true"}

return_values.name: vpc_id
return_values.description: ID for the VPC in which the route lives. Returned: always Sample: "vpc-6e2d2407"
